C1.rationale: Emphasises persuasive verbal and non-verbal business communication, cross-cultural team leadership, and pitching proposals to critical executive stakeholders (MGMT2100, MGMT3027).
evidenceLines: There is a strong focus on the understanding the theory of communication in the business context and it's application to effective business writing at a high level, persuasive and appropriate verbal and non verbal communication, and interpersonal skills across teams and cultures.
Present a persuasive business plan to potential investors or to internal stakeholders and effectively answer probing questions on the substance of the plan; and,

C2.rationale: Requires creative thinking and entrepreneurial venture design, formulating original commercial strategies and novel business models (MGMT3027).
evidenceLines: The course focuses on the skills necessary for the planning, development and launch of entrepreneurial and innovative ventures. The material covered includes the foundations of entrepreneurship, techniques for creative thinking, and processes for developing, planning and launching a new venture including protecting intellectual property, evaluating markets, developing innovative business models, budgeting, and raising finance.
Develop a comprehensive and well structured business plan for a new venture;

C3.rationale: Rigorous strategic decision analysis, evaluating internal capabilities against dynamic macroeconomic and competitor pressures to determine optimal strategic trajectories (MGMT3015).
evidenceLines: Analyse an organisation’s internal and external environments by applying appropriate theories, models, and/or frameworks;
Formulate appropriate strategies to gain a competitive advantage at both business and corporate levels;

C4.rationale: Trains managers in strategic adaptation and evidence gathering under conditions of high market uncertainty, ambiguity, and rapidly changing consumer dynamics (MKTG2004, MGMT2003).
evidenceLines: industry analysis, buyer behaviour in the consumer and business organisations, and decision making under conditions of high uncertainty and ambiguity.

Gathering and interpreting information is critical to business decision-making. Having a firm grasp of business research methods can enable managers and business leaders to make better decisions and to solve problems more effectively.

C5.rationale: Involves in-person formal presentation delivery and pitching with live questioning, but lacks intensive manual dexterity or physical site interaction requirements (MGMT2100, MGMT3027).
evidenceLines: apply communication theory in delivering an effective business presentation
Present a persuasive business plan to potential investors or to internal stakeholders and effectively answer probing questions on the substance of the plan; and,

W1.rationale: Engages with live commercial case studies and demands full-scale business plan development mirroring authentic enterprise management (MKTG2004, MGMT3027).
evidenceLines: Identify marketing problems from live case studies;
The major piece of assessment is the writing of a comprehensive business plan.

W2.rationale: Examines ethical employer obligations, equity and diversity management, workplace health and safety regulations, and fair employment relations (MGMT2030).
evidenceLines: Specific topics include the strategic role of HRM, recruitment and selection, learning and career development, employee motivation and reward management, performance appraisal, diversity management, workplace health and safety, and employment relations.
Apply academic research to people management issues in organisations to generate solutions;

W3.rationale: Integrates statutory Australian industrial relations, intellectual property protections, commercial financial frameworks, and venture capital budgeting mechanisms (MGMT2030, MGMT3027).
evidenceLines: processes for developing, planning and launching a new venture including protecting intellectual property, evaluating markets, developing innovative business models, budgeting, and raising finance.
Identify the major concepts, principles and issues related to Human Resource strategy and practice in Australia from the perspective of both organisational needs and the employee lifecycle;

G1.rationale: Program satisfies foundational discipline depth requirements.
evidenceLines: Specifically, the topics of this class are designed to enhance students’ appreciation of self-understanding and development (managerial roles, personality, decision-making), interpersonal dynamics and communication (motivation, social influence, group decision-making, leadership, cross-cultural management), and organisational features (i.e., social dilemma, organisational culture) that altogether build foundation and confidence as future managers and leaders.

G2.rationale: Program satisfies contextual professional and analytical practice requirements.
evidenceLines: The course draws upon case studies to highlight key concepts in strategic decision-making.
